# Final tables (generated by `experiments/phase7/7c_tables.py`)

Every number below is read from `results/final/final_results.json`, which `7a_final_results.py` builds from the Phase 3-6 result and handoff files (source file and key stored per value), or read directly from the result file named in the table. Nothing is typed by hand except labels. All beam metrics: 2-D lossless model, validated band 0.231-0.268, res 30 production, theta0 = 30 deg.

## Table 2. Phase-by-phase validation summary

| phase | question | method | result (from files) | restriction passed on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | which 2-D geometry family | MPB screening, pre-declared rule | triangular air holes, TE, W1 (moderate-margin decision; r/a = 0.30 is a post-selection engineering choice) | decision rests on slow-light potential and FDTD cost |
| 1 | is the FDTD delay/transfer extraction trustworthy | vacuum, dielectric, Bragg vs TMM, 2-D crystal vs MPB | vacuum delay error 2.24e-03 a/c at res 40, second-order convergence; Bragg and slab agree with TMM at measured order about 2; 2-D stop-band edges within 3.5e-3 of MPB | tolerance 3.5e-3 is dominated by finite length/termination |
| 2 | does finite W1 FDTD reproduce MPB n_g | modal projection, 3-length fit, tol 1e-7 | in 0.231-0.268 (res 40): median bias +0.27 %, max |dn_g| 1.00 % | upper edge 0.268 chosen post hoc; tol 1e-6 not usable |
| 3 | does dispersion engineering of the first rows pay | D0/D1/D2 FDTD, N = 4, 8, 12 | D0 flat-delay band 14.8 %, D1 8.4 %, D2 5.6 %; D0 selected | three-point illustration; bands bounded by validated range; sign bug fixed and rerun |
| 4 | four-channel delay family | N = 8-11 direct FDTD | band-fit increments 3.9315, 3.9308, 3.9310 a/c (max 0.038 % off target); amplitude imbalance 0.023 dB; raw intercept error up to 2.67 rad; trimmed residual 0.026 rad | first attempt discarded (under-converged); estimator changed post hoc |
| 5 | element-level 4-element array | actual H_m as weights | trimmed PhC within 0.050 deg of ideal TTD; fixed phase squints 2.69 deg; but d = 1.96 lambda0 gives equal-strength grating lobes (0.0 dB) | quantum 0.981 cycle forces sparse array |
| 6 | delay-granularity mitigation | hierarchical subarrays Msub = 1, 2, 4, 8; system-level Monte Carlo | Msub = 4: mismatch -1.89 %, max error 0.189 deg, R_squint 0.070, strongest sidelobe -12.4 dB, replica lobe -16.6 dB | one angle; constant trim required; replica lobes remain |

## Table 3. D0 / D1 / D2 trade study (FDTD, res 30, validated range, +-10 % flat-delay band)

| design | band | fractional BW | median delay per period (a/c) | GBP | GDD per period, band avg (a/c)^2 | periods for 25 cycles | R max | T min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D0 | 0.2310-0.2680 | 14.8 % | 3.932 | 0.583 | -0.91 | 25.5 | 0.0026 | 0.991 |
| D1 | 0.2465-0.2680 | 8.4 % | 4.204 | 0.351 | -3.86 | 23.1 | 0.0073 | 0.990 |
| D2 | 0.2535-0.2680 | 5.6 % | 4.469 | 0.248 | -7.07 | 21.5 | 0.0100 | 0.987 |

The band ends at 0.268 for every design: the validated-range edge, not delay flatness, bounds the high side (and 0.231 bounds D0 on the low side). D1/D2 differ from D0 in the first hole row only (radius factor 1.2, shift -0.05 / -0.10).

|---|---|

| T range | 0.9969-1.0025 (excess over 1 is numerical) |

| trimmed phase residual, max by channel (m = 0..3) | 0.0000, 0.0086, 0.0172, 0.0260 rad (1.49 deg max) |

Pointwise delay increments (local fits) vary by several percent across the band (Figure 4b); only the band-fit increments are within 0.04 % of target. The trimmed channels are not ideal TTD: the residual is mostly curvature of n_g(f).

## Table 5. Phase 5 element-level array vs Phase 6 Msub = 4 subarray architecture

| metric | Phase 5: 4 elements, d = 1.96 lambda0 | Phase 6: 16 elements, Msub = 4 |
|---|---|---|
| fixed-phase max pointing error | 2.69 deg | 2.69 deg |
| ideal TTD max pointing error | 3.8e-12 deg (element-level) | 0.156 deg (ideal subarray TTD) |
| raw PhC max pointing error | 6.81 deg | 6.68 deg |
| trimmed PhC max pointing error | 0.050 deg | 0.189 deg |
| trimmed PhC R_squint | 0.019 | 0.070 |
| strongest other lobe | 0.0 dB (grating lobes) | -12.4 dB (ordinary sidelobe) |
| strongest subarray replica lobe | not applicable | -16.6 dB |
| HPBW low / f0 / high | 8.30 / 7.69 / 7.16 deg | 7.95 / 7.35 / 6.83 deg |
| minimum peak power | 0.9978 | 0.9829 (-0.075 dB) |

The Phase 5 trimmed-PhC error is smaller than the Phase 6 one because the Phase 6 array adds fixed intra-subarray phases that squint even for ideal subarray TTD (0.156 deg); the PhC adds 0.055 deg on top. The two aperture designs are not directly comparable in pointing error; the comparison that matters is the lobe structure.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.250 | 3.9244 | +292.4 % | 7.671 | 2.855 | -4.8 |
| 2 | 0.500 | 1.9622 | +96.2 % | 2.367 | 0.881 | -12.2 |

## Table 6. Robustness / system-level tolerance estimates (Msub = 4; not fabrication tolerances)

| item | value |
|---|---|
| nominal max pointing error | 0.189 deg |
| combined L2 test (phase +-2 deg, delay +-0.5 %, amplitude +-0.25 dB): P95 max error | 0.352 deg |
| phase-trim error giving P95 = 0.5 deg / 1.0 deg | +-7.6 deg / +-20.1 deg |
| uncalibrated delay error (of q x tau_PhC) giving P95 = 0.5 deg / 1.0 deg | +-1.17 % / +-2.94 % |
| res 30 vs res 40: max change of design-lobe angle (limit) | 0.0070 deg (0.122 deg) |
| res 30 vs res 40: change of R_squint / strongest lobe | 0.0005 / 0.041 dB |
| Phase 4 trim used unchanged (not re-trimmed to 4.008 a) | max error 0.73 deg (exceeds tracking tolerance 0.37 deg) |

Uncalibrated absolute-length errors are severe (about 0.14 % of the whole device delay for P95 = 0.5 deg, Phase 6 report Section 5): a length error is benign only if the constant phase is re-trimmed afterward. Perturbations are mathematical, uniform and independent per channel; no fabrication-disorder FDTD was run.

## Table 7. Restrictions and unresolved issues

| # | restriction | consequence for the claim |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2-D, lossless, uniform dielectric; no propagation loss, disorder, coupling, bends, thermal effects, realistic couplers | no claim of loss performance, fabrication readiness or 3-D validity |
| 2 | validated band 0.231-0.268 (14.8 %); upper edge 0.268 chosen post hoc in Phase 2 | bandwidth is a domain-limited lower bound, not a measured band edge |
| 3 | Phase 4: first FDTD attempt discarded (under-convergence); common minimum run time 3500 added after seeing data; increment estimator changed post hoc | delay claims rest on phase slopes and band fits; pointwise increments are noisy |
| 4 | constant phase-intercept trim required per channel (raw intercept error up to 2.7 rad) | the channels are TTD slope plus a fixed phase, not TTD alone; how the trim is realized is not addressed |
| 5 | subarray replica lobes remain (strongest -16.6 dB); fixed intra-subarray phase leaves +-0.16 deg squint even for ideal subarray TTD | grating-lobe problem mitigated, not eliminated |
| 6 | one steering angle (30 deg) and one match (Msub = 4, one-period step) | the 1.9 % match is a coincidence of n_g x f0 about 0.98 at this angle; other angles need other designs |
| 7 | Msub = 8 with two-period steps not simulated; only four channels, one flat-n_g mode at four lengths | no claim about larger families |
| 8 | robustness is system-level (mathematical perturbations on the measured H_q) | not fabrication tolerances |
| 9 | no conventional-delay-line comparison at the subarray level; Phase 3 reference R is MPB-only | no quantified advantage over conventional lines beyond MPB group-index/footprint |
| 10 | carrier-delay mapping only: the PhC delays the radiated carrier | does not describe RF-photonic beamforming |
| 11 | no experiment; literature positioning not done | no novelty claim |
